anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

choices.why: The fault is jumping at a Greek pun before knowing Hebrew.
Origen's regular word for those who know fully.

pass_a_gloss: And if someone of ours rather rashly, meeting Hebrews, should say the pascha was so named because of the Savior's passion, he will be laughable to them as wholly not knowing what is signified from the naming, if they should interpret the pascha-name properly as the perfect Hebrews do.
pass_b_english: And if one of our people, rather rashly, should meet with Hebrews and say that the Passover was so named because of the passion of the Savior, he will be laughed at by them as one who does not know at all what is signified by the name — if they should interpret the name of the Passover properly, as the perfect among the Hebrews do.
source_text: Καὶ εἴ τις προπετέστερον τῶν ἡμετέρων Ἑβραίοις συμβαλὼν λέγοι τὸ πάσχα διὰ τὸ πάθος τοῦ σ(ωτῆ)ρ(ο)ς οὕτως ὠνομάσθαι, καταγέλαστος ὑπ’ αὐτῶν ἔσται ὡς ὅλως οὐκ ἐ||πιστάμενος τί τὸ σημαιν<όμενο>ν ἐκ τῆς ὀνομασίας, εἰ κυρίως ὡς Ἑβραῖοι οἱ τέλειοι τὸ τοῦ πάσχα ἑρμηνεύσαιεν ὄνομα.
